front: In a PROFINET system, what does the IO-Controller do?
back: It controls the automation task and one or more field devices.
excerpt: A minimal Profinet IO-System consists of at least one IO-Controller that controls one or more IO-Devices.

front: In a PROFINET system, what is an IO-Device?
back: A field device, such as an I/O block, drive, sensor or actuator, that an IO-Controller monitors and controls.
excerpt: which is a field device, monitored and controlled by an IO-Controller. An IO-Device may consist of several modules and sub-modules.

front: What does a GSD (General Station Description) file do in PROFINET engineering?
back: It holds the manufacturer's description of an IO-Device's properties, which the engineering tool uses to plan the system configuration.
excerpt: The GSD file serves an engineering environment as a basis for planning the configuration of a Profinet IO system.

front: How are PROFINET Real-Time (RT) telegrams with cyclic data and alarms carried on the network?
back: Directly via Ethernet; the User Datagram Protocol over Internet Protocol is used for acyclic data instead.
excerpt: For real-time data (cyclic data and alarms), the Profinet Real-Time (RT) telegrams are transmitted directly via Ethernet. UDP/IP is used for the transmission of acyclic data.

front: PROFINET RT reaches cycle times of 1-10 ms. What does Isochronous Real-Time (IRT) add?
back: Cycle times below 1 ms, as needed by drive technology applications.
excerpt: The IRT (Isochronous Real-Time) protocol for application class C allows cycle times below 1 ms for drive technology applications.

front: How does PROFINET Isochronous Real-Time (IRT) keep ordinary Ethernet traffic from delaying its real-time data?
back: Bandwidth reservation: each fixed cycle is split into phases, and one phase is reserved exclusively for IRT real-time data.
excerpt: The bandwidth is divided into fixed cycle times, which in turn are divided into phases. The red phase is reserved exclusively for class C real-time data
mnemonic: A traffic light for frames: the red phase is for IRT data only, the green phase lets ordinary Ethernet through.

front: Which application protocol does EtherNet/IP adapt to run on standard Ethernet?
excerpt: EtherNet/IP (IP = Industrial Protocol) is an industrial network protocol that adapts the Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) to standard Ethernet.
mnemonic: The IP in EtherNet/IP means Industrial Protocol: the Common Industrial Protocol riding on Ethernet.

front: In EtherNet/IP, what is explicit messaging used for?
back: Uploading and downloading parameters, setpoints, programs and recipes.
excerpt: Uploading and downloading of parameters, setpoints, programs and recipes via TCP (i.e., explicit messaging.)

front: EtherNet/IP uses Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) port 44818 and User Datagram Protocol (UDP) port 2222. Which one carries implicit messaging, the basic input/output data?
excerpt: EtherNet/IP makes use of TCP port number 44818 for explicit messaging and UDP port number 2222 for implicit messaging

front: What is OPC Unified Architecture (OPC UA) for?
back: Standardized, cross-platform data exchange all the way from sensors up to cloud applications.
excerpt: OPC Unified Architecture (OPC UA) is a cross-platform, open-source, IEC62541 standard for data exchange from sensors to cloud applications developed by the OPC Foundation.

front: How does an OPC UA server organize the information it offers to clients?
back: As a mesh of nodes, similar to objects in object-oriented programming, that hold process data together with metadata.
excerpt: These nodes can include any kind of meta information, and are similar to the objects of object-oriented programming (OOP).

front: In OPC UA, how does message security mode Sign differ from SignAndEncrypt?
back: Sign only signs every message; SignAndEncrypt signs and also encrypts every message.
excerpt: SIGN 2 All messages are signed but not encrypted. SIGNANDENCRYPT 3 All messages are signed and encrypted.
mnemonic: Sign is a sealed but transparent envelope; SignAndEncrypt is sealed and opaque.
